items.title: Defamation case against Rahul Gandhi: Savarkar kin says cross-examination causing mental agony; seeks strict timeline
items.summary: Satyaki Savarkar, grandnephew of VD Savarkar, has moved a Pune court seeking a strict timeline and tighter control over the ongoing cross-examination in his criminal defamation case against leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi. In an application filed on July 30, Savarkar alleged that his cross-examination by Gandhi's lawyer has stretched over seven months, causing him severe harassment and mental agony. After considering the application on August 4, Judicial magistrate Amol Shinde sought Gandhi’s response. It will now be considered on the next date of hearing on August 14. The application pointed out that Savarkar’s examination-in-chief concluded on December 31, 2025. The same day, his cross-examination by defence began and that is ongoing since the past seven months. “It is evidence that Gandhi has adopted dilatory tactic to prolong the matter. A multitude of the questions being asked as merely repetitive and irrelevant as they address topics that neither form the subject matter of the criminal case, nor were they mentioned in the complainant’s examination-in-chief,” it was submitted. items.title: TN Secretariat union objects Rs 14,000 crore pension allocation cuts
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Tamil Nadu Secretariat Association has written to Chief Minister Vijay expressing their objection to the reduction of the allocation for pensions and retirement benefits in the state’s first full Budget presented by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government. In its representation to the Chief Minister on Thursday, August 6, the association said the reduction of nearly Rs 14,000 crore in pension-related allocations for government employees and teachers, had come as a “major shock” at a time when government employees and teachers were expecting the new government to restore the Old Pension Scheme (OPS). The Budget for 2026-27 was presented in the Assembly by the Finance Minister Marie Wilson on August 5. According to the association, the total allocation under various pension and retirement benefits has been reduced from Rs 57,207.16 crore in the interim Budget estimates for 2026-27 to Rs 43,203.81 crore in the revised Budget estimates with a decline of Rs 14,003.32 crore.
